summary: Bengaluru cloud engineer, 2.5 yrs, joined as a fresher. Collects certificates fast (nine in 22 months, most as uploaded PDFs) and does short Udemy runs, while the actual work in infra-live is small tagging, tfvars and copy-adapted IAM or cron changes with heavy reviewer rewriting. A bright junior who is a level or two below what the CV and profile say.
archetype: certificate collector with thin hands-on work

skills.why: Does bounded AWS changes in Terraform (tags, SG, alarms, a Lambda scheduler) with visible reviewer corrections; three AWS certs verified, but practical depth is guided work.
Edits modules and tfvars; IAM PR was reworked by reviewers after a copy-paste revert; no module authoring or state repair.
Edits helm values and resource limits; scored low on a fundamentals test; CKAD document failed verification.
Course runs only; no Dockerfile work in the record.
Kestrel runs on AWS; Azure knowledge comes from study and a lapsed associate cert, no workplace Azure use.
Only an unverifiable PDF; nothing in work systems and no course trail.
Extends an existing GitHub Actions workflow for plan-on-PR with review.
Routine admin and access tasks; no kernel or tuning evidence.
Adds CloudWatch alarms from templates; no dashboards design.

decoys.why: CV only; one helm values bump for a Grafana pod is not usage

traps.plant: Six of nine certificates are PDF uploads; one (CKAD) fails lookup, others unverifiable; the verified three are all AWS
CV rates Kubernetes and Terraform as Advanced; GCP and Azure listed as cloud experience; work evidence does not support it
Azure admin associate lapsed in 2026-01 yet listed without date on the CV
Udemy courses of 25+ hours show 35-130 minutes spent, completed same week
Self-declared level 3 on five cloud skills in Jan 2026
Associate Cloud Engineer certificate (PDF) only; no work

answer_behavior.notes: Says yes to levels up to 3 on everything cloud; eager and responsive.
